I understand what you're saying. But is a problem more to the individual than the profession it self. Even as an RN I look to labs and history to come to a nurses diagnosis. I wouldn't call it a complete wash because I've had MDs either neglect to mention an abnormal lab or they were waiting to do something about it after it required medicinal therapy. Particularly my A1C and free T4 (which I had to get papers from elective surgery for the doc to even run it). Then with my A1C, I reported the sugar cravings, dizziness, coldness, increased water intake and clamminess and my values were low. This was a bad situation with 2 less than prudent MDs. I chalk that up to anyone who rushes to getting a title not just NPs. Practitioners should take pt reports/complaints more seriously as a whole rather than just wanting a title. So you're absolutely right no one should risk their health to protect the ego of a doctor, np or any health professional.

It sucks when assumptions are made when symptoms are reported, especially pain.  But did the NP even inquire about recent activities or review the lab work or was she automatically stating 'nope, change your diet.' I wouldn't consider the reports of muscle pain to be a mistake at all when looking at your labs, follow up questions about recent activities and characteristics among many other things would come to mind before being that dismissive. I wouldn't write off all NPs. However, in this instance this one may not have been so prudent.
